rc-01.label: The free-text field that allowed users to submit arbitrary prompts to the underlying model is removed; only a fixed set of actions remains.
rc-01.why: The injection surface is gone, not guarded. Elimination is recognisable because the mitigation removes a capability rather than constraining its use.

rc-02.label: The feature that inferred demographic attributes from user photos is deleted from the product.
rc-02.why: No inference means no inference error, no disparate accuracy and no lawful-basis question. The hazard is not managed; it no longer exists.

rc-03.label: A chatbot's ability to execute account changes is withdrawn entirely; it can now only read and explain.
rc-03.why: Removing the write capability eliminates the entire class of unauthorised-action harms. Everything downstream of it becomes unnecessary.

rc-04.label: Direct identifiers are dropped from the training corpus altogether rather than being protected within it.
rc-04.why: Data that was never collected cannot leak, be re-identified, or be subject to an access request. This is why minimisation outranks encryption.

rc-05.label: A generative model used for summarising medical notes is replaced with an extractive summariser that can only quote the source.
rc-05.why: The purpose is preserved while the hazardous mechanism — free generation, and therefore fabrication — is swapped out for one that cannot fabricate.

rc-06.label: A black-box gradient-boosted model in a lending decision is replaced by a monotonic scorecard with comparable accuracy.
rc-06.why: Redesigning for an inherently explainable model removes the explanation problem rather than bolting a post-hoc explainer onto it.

rc-07.label: Real customer records used in a test environment are replaced with synthetic data of the same statistical shape.
rc-07.why: The activity continues with a materially safer input. Substitution sits below elimination because the replacement carries its own, smaller risks.

rc-08.label: A facial recognition step in an identity check is replaced with a document-plus-liveness check that does not build a face template.
rc-08.why: Same assurance objective, different mechanism, far lower biometric exposure. The tell is that the function survives and the hazard is exchanged.

rc-09.label: Output filters block responses containing personal data patterns before they ever reach the user.
rc-09.why: The constraint is enforced by the system on every request. Nobody has to remember it, which is what makes technical controls outrank procedural ones.

rc-10.label: Role-based access control prevents the retrieval layer from returning documents the requesting user is not entitled to see.
rc-10.why: Authorisation is enforced at the point of retrieval rather than trusted to the prompt. A rule the system applies cannot be forgotten under pressure.

rc-11.label: A hard cap limits the number of tool calls an agent may make before it must stop and escalate.
rc-11.why: A runtime bound holds regardless of what the model decides to do. Improving the tool description would be an administrative measure by comparison.

rc-12.label: Deployment is gated by an automated evaluation suite that fails the build if subgroup performance regresses beyond a threshold.
rc-12.why: The gate is mechanical and cannot be skipped by a busy release manager, which is precisely why it beats a review checklist covering the same ground.

rc-13.label: An acceptable-use policy is published and all staff complete annual training on it.
rc-13.why: Effectiveness depends entirely on people reading, remembering and applying it. Training is worth having and is routinely over-credited in risk assessments.

rc-14.label: A procedure requires a second reviewer to sign off on every high-impact model change.
rc-14.why: A procedural gate can be bypassed under deadline pressure. Making the same check a required status in the pipeline would move it up a tier.

rc-15.label: Quarterly manual audits sample model decisions and check them against policy.
rc-15.why: Detective, periodic and human. It finds problems after they occur, which is useful and is not prevention.

rc-16.label: An incident response runbook sets out who is called and in what order when a model misbehaves.
rc-16.why: Procedural preparation reduces impact through faster response, but only if the procedure is followed and current.

rc-17.label: A notice on screen warns people that answers come from an AI system and could contain errors.
rc-17.why: A disclosure obligation may well be mandatory, but as mitigation it is the weakest tier: it transfers vigilance to the user, who cannot inspect the model.

rc-18.label: The interface warns users not to enter confidential information into the assistant.
rc-18.why: The warning depends on the person least equipped to enforce it. Blocking sensitive patterns at input would be an engineering control for the same risk.

rc-19.label: Documentation states that the model was not validated for use on paediatric cases.
rc-19.why: Stating a limitation informs the deployer without preventing the misuse. Refusing out-of-scope inputs at runtime would be materially stronger.

rc-20.label: Generated images carry a visible label and embedded provenance metadata identifying them as synthetic.
rc-20.why: Provenance marking supports downstream judgement and is often legally required. It changes nothing about what the system will produce.

risk-controls.hint: Drag each mitigation onto its tier. The question is how much the measure depends on a human doing the right thing — the more it does, the weaker the tier.
risk-controls.note: The order matters more than the labels. A measure that depends on a person reading, remembering and complying is structurally weaker than one that makes the failure impossible, however diligently the first is written.
risk-controls.zones[0].def: Remove the hazard. The failure mode cannot occur because the capability that produced it is gone.
risk-controls.zones[1].def: Replace the hazardous element with a safer one that achieves the same purpose.
risk-controls.zones[2].def: Build the constraint into the system so that it holds without anyone choosing to comply.
risk-controls.zones[3].def: Policies, training, review steps and procedures. Effective only to the extent people follow them.
risk-controls.zones[4].def: Tell the user. The weakest tier: it moves responsibility to the person least able to change the outcome.
